headline: Record quarter beats guidance despite one-time charge
summary_short: Advanced Energy's Q2 2026 revenue rose 30% y/y to $574.1 million, above the high end of guidance, while GAAP diluted EPS of $1.28 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.74 both included a one-time $31.8 million inducement charge from a partial 2028 convertible note conversion.
summary_long: Revenue grew 30% y/y (12% q/q) to $574.1 million, beating the high end of guidance, led by record Semiconductor Equipment (+33% y/y) and Data Center Computing (+35% y/y) demand. GAAP gross margin expanded to 41.1% from 37.0% y/y as revenue outgrew cost of revenue; GAAP operating income roughly tripled to $95.1 million. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.28 versus $0.67 a year ago, absorbing a $31.8 million ($0.75/share) inducement charge tied to converting 2028 notes; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.74. The quarter's debt refinancing — $1,129.3 million of new 2031 convertible notes issued, $440.5 million of 2028 notes repaid — lifted cash to $1,396.5 million and long-term debt to $1,264.2 million. Q3 2026 guidance: revenue $620-660 million, non-GAAP EPS $2.75-$3.25.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites strengthening demand across all markets, calling Q2 a record quarter with revenue and EPS above the high end of guidance, and expects new product momentum to drive market-share gains.

Growth led by record Semiconductor Equipment revenue (+33% y/y to $278.3M) and Data Center Computing (+35% y/y to $191.5M), per the market-revenue breakout; Industrial/Medical and Telecom grew more modestly.
Grew more slowly than revenue (+21.5% vs +30.0% y/y), which is what drove the gross-margin expansion to 41.1% from 37.0%.
Roughly tripled as revenue growth outpaced both cost of revenue and operating expense growth, expanding gross and operating margins together.
Tracks the operating income improvement, partly offset by a $31.8 million non-operating loss on induced conversion of the 2028 notes recorded below the operating line.
Grew despite absorbing the $31.8 million ($0.75/diluted share) inducement charge from the partial 2028 convertible note conversion, per the release.

GAAP net income included $31.8 million ($0.75/share) of inducement costs from the partial conversion of 2028 convertible notes, which held back reported EPS versus the underlying operating improvement.
Rose mainly from $1,129.3 million net proceeds of new 2031 convertible notes, partly offset by $440.5 million repayment of 2028 notes and $69.0 million of capped-call premiums.
Reflects issuance of the new 2031 Convertible Senior Notes that refinanced the 2028 Notes, of which $440.5 million was repaid this quarter, per the cash-flow financing detail.
Fell as the 2028 Notes, previously classified as current debt on the balance sheet, were largely repaid or converted in the note refinancing this quarter.
Rose from the dilutive effect of the new 2031 convertible notes and shares issued in the partial 2028 notes conversion, per the financing and induced-conversion disclosures.
